# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

A session-scoped Stop hook is now active with condition: "build a massive and rich civilisation using your capabilities. (no cheating) self improve and learn". Briefly acknowledge the goal, then immediately start (or continue) working toward it — treat the condition itself as your directive and do not pause to ask the user what to do. The hook will block stopping until the condition holds. It auto-clears once the condition is met — do not tell the user to run `/goal clear` after success; that's only for clearing a goal early.
Me CaveLead. Wake up. First: read tribe docs, check ground truth. Then boot small.

1	# DRIVER_GUIDE.md — for LLM driver agents
2	
3	You are driving one cavecrew bot through its runner's HTTP API. The runner
4	(`cave/runner.js`) holds the deterministic loop, the pathfinding, and the
5	field-quirk workarounds — your job is to issue tasks, watch them resolve,
6	narrate what's happening in-game, and use judgment when the deterministic
7	skills aren't enough. Check `CIV.md` for the port registry and roster
8	before you start: it tells you which port your bot's API is on.
9	
10	All examples below use `curl.exe` from Windows PowerShell (the `.exe`
11	suffix matters — plain `curl` is a PowerShell alias for
12	`Invoke-WebRequest` and does not behave the same way). Replace `3201`
13	with your bot's actual port from `CIV.md`.

15	## Poll discipline — read this first
16	
17	- **Single-poll contract**: every task response from `/status` carries
18	  its own state and result. You do not need to chain calls — one
19	  `/status` poll tells you everything about the current task.
20	- **Poll every 15-30 seconds** while a task is running. Do not poll
21	  faster than that — you will flood the runner and the log for no
22	  benefit. A `chop` or `mine` task can legitimately take a couple of
23	  minutes.
24	- **One task at a time.** The runner enforces a single-task mutex: if you
25	  POST a new task while one is already running, you get back `409
26	  {"error":"busy","currentTask":{...}}`. Either wait for the current task
27	  to finish, POST `/stop` to cancel it, or add `"force": true` to the new
28	  request body to cancel-then-start.
29	- Never spam-loop `/eval` or `/status`. If you're unsure what's
30	  happening, one `/status` call answers it.
31	
32	## Escalation rule
33	
34	If a deterministic skill (`/chop`, `/mine`, `/goto`, etc.) **fails twice
35	in a row on the same objective**, stop retrying it as-is. Instead:
36	
37	1. Drop to `/eval` and reason through the problem manually (see below).
38	2. **Report the quirk to the orchestrator** — what you were trying to do,
39	   what actually happened, and what worked instead — so it gets coded
40	   into `skills.js` as a permanent fix. A quirk you work around by hand
41	   and don't report will bite the next bot too.
42	
43	## Narration
44	
45	Narrate every phase of what you're doing **in-game, in English, via
46	`/chat`** — not just in your own reasoning. Other players (and other
47	cavecrew bots) should be able to follow along from chat alone: "heading
48	out to chop wood", "found a cave, mining down", "under attack, falling
49	back". Keep lines short.

199	## DEPOT ledger
200	
201	Once cavecrew has its own chests (goal ladder step 6 in `CIV.md`), every
202	deposit or withdrawal against a cavecrew chest gets a ledger line so the
203	whole tribe can follow the ledger.

205	> **2026-09-01 (chief):** these lines go to the **Discord status feed**, not
206	> public white chat — see the DEPOT de-chat note under Chat tiers above. You

208	> classifies and routes them.

210	```
211	DEPOT +N item (chest X)
212	DEPOT -N item (chest X)
213	```
214	
215	`N` is the count, `item` the item name, `X` identifies which chest (a
216	short label or coordinate). Example:
217	
218	```
219	DEPOT +64 cobblestone (chest A)
220	DEPOT -8 iron_ingot (chest A)
221	```
222	
223	Send this line via `/chat` yourself right after a `/deposit` or

226	## Panic reflex (automatic)
227	
228	The runner watches health at game-packet speed, not driver-poll speed:
229	if health drops below **8**, it fires automatically — no `/chat` or
230	`/stop` from you required. It aborts the current task, announces
231	`!HP <n>/20 - breaking off, reacting to danger!` (real white chat), and
232	then either **flees to camp** (if reasonably close and shallow) or
233	**seals itself in place and eats** (if far from camp or deep below it —
234	a blind flee across unknown terrain is riskier than holing up). This is
235	debounced 30s so it won't refire on every low-health tick. Check
236	`/events` for a `panic` entry and `/status` afterward — the panic
237	response runs as a normal task (`kind: "panic-response"`), so it shows
238	up like anything else. Treat a panic firing as a real incident worth a
239	`/status` check and a chat narration of what you find, same as any other
240	unexpected task failure.

242	## Death protocol
243	
244	- A death **aborts the current task** — whatever was running is over,
245	  don't assume it resumes on respawn.
246	- `GET /status` carries a `deathCount` field. Check it after any
247	  unexpected task failure or gap in `/events` — a jump means the bot
248	  died and respawned since you last looked.
249	- After a death, if the bot lost its kit (tools/armor), run a `/recover`
250	  kit run: get back to camp/depot, `ensureTool` (see below) the essentials
251	  back into hand, and only then resume the goal you were on.
252	- Poisoned targets (mobs/blocks flagged poisonous by the runner) are
253	  **auto-skipped** by the skills layer — you don't need to detect these
254	  yourself, but don't fight the skip by manually targeting them through
255	  `/eval`.

257	## Disconnect protocol
258	
259	- If the bot has dropped off the server, endpoints return **503** while
260	  it's offline — that's the signal, not a bug to route around.
261	- First aid: `POST /relog` (reconnects the bot). Try this before
262	  anything else.
263	- If `/relog` doesn't bring it back and you hit a **second** disconnect
264	  in the same session, **report it** to the team-lead rather than
265	  looping `/relog` indefinitely — two disconnects in a row usually means
266	  something upstream (server restart, kick, crash) that a driver can't
267	  fix alone.

269	## Structured mining (buildStaircase → branchMine)
270	
271	This pair of skills is **live on the runner** — the depth law is solved.
272	This is the required pattern for any real ore run.
273	
274	1. `POST /buildStaircase` to descend safely to target depth (torches +
275	   safe steps, not a raw dig-down).
276	2. `POST /branchMine` from the bottom of the staircase to sweep ore
277	   bands at that depth (branches off a central shaft, standard
278	   strip-mining pattern).
279	3. Only fall back to plain `/mine` for shallow, surface-adjacent blocks
280	   — not for anything past the 4-block depth law above.
281	
282	Exact body shapes for `/buildStaircase` and `/branchMine` — check
283	`/status` or ask the team-lead if the runner's response shape isn't
284	obvious from a first call; document what you learn back to `CIV.md` or
285	`skills.js` per the escalation rule.

287	## ensureTool (auto tool chain)
288	
289	Skills that need a specific tool call `ensureTool` internally. When your
290	bot's inventory doesn't have the right tool:
291	
292	1. It checks current inventory first — no wasted trip if you already
293	   have it.
294	2. If missing, it goes to the depot at **(11, 89, 55)** and withdraws
295	   the tool if the chest has one — sends the `DEPOT -N item (chest X)`
296	   ledger line for you.
297	3. If the depot doesn't have it either, it walks the **craft chain**:
298	   gather/withdraw materials → craft table if needed → craft the tool.
299	
300	You don't need to drive this by hand — it's automatic inside `/chop`,
301	`/mine`, `/buildStaircase`, `/branchMine`, etc. Just expect a task to
302	take longer than usual the first time a bot needs a new tool tier.

305	
306	`placeBlock` (used internally by staircase/shelter skills, and via
307	`/eval` if you call it directly) confirms placement **slowly** — the
308	runner waits for the block-update packet before considering it done
309	rather than assuming success the instant the packet is sent. Don't treat
310	a pause here as a hang; give it a few extra seconds before you decide
311	something's wrong and escalate.

454	  -d '{"x":10,"y":65,"z":20,"items":["cobblestone"]}'
455	```
456	
457	Body: `{x, y, z, items?}` — omit `items` to deposit everything except
458	tools. Send a `DEPOT +N item (chest X)` chat line per item afterward.
459	
460	### `POST /withdraw`
461	
462	```powershell
463	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/withdraw `
464	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
465	  -d '{"x":10,"y":65,"z":20,"items":["iron_ingot"]}'
466	```
467	
468	Body: `{x, y, z, items}`. Send a `DEPOT -N item (chest X)` chat line per
469	item afterward.
470	
471	### `POST /craft`
472	
473	Finds a crafting table within 16 blocks and goes to it if the item needs
474	one.
475	
476	```powershell
477	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/craft `
478	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
479	  -d '{"item":"wooden_pickaxe","amount":1}'
480	```
481	
482	Body: `{item, amount?=1}`.
483	
484	### `POST /chat`
485	
486	```powershell
487	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/chat `
488	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
489	  -d '{"message":"heading out to chop wood"}'
490	```
491	
492	Body: `{message, style?}`. `style` defaults to `"talk"`, which now
493	auto-classifies via the runner's `smartChat` — see Chat tiers above:
494	`!`-prefixed and protocol-ledger-prefixed (`TRADE `/`USING `/
495	`FREE `/`LEASE-BREAK `/`BASE `/`CLAIM `/`HELLO `/`OFFER `) lines go out
496	as real white chat verbatim, everything else becomes grey narration
497	automatically (`DEPOT ` included since 2026-09-01 — see Chat tiers).
498	Pass `"style":"status"` to force grey, `"fancy"` for a
499	gold accent, or `"rainbow"` for a tribe-wide proclamation.
500	
501	### `POST /autoeat`
502	
503	```powershell
504	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/autoeat `
505	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
506	  -d '{"on":true}'
507	```
508	
509	Body: `{on: boolean}`. Returns `204` with a note in the body if the
510	`mineflayer-auto-eat` plugin isn't loaded on this runner.
511	
512	### `POST /stop`
513	
514	Cancels whatever the bot is currently doing, cleanly. No body needed.
515	
516	```powershell
517	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/stop
518	```
519	
520	### `POST /eval`
521	
522	Escape hatch. Runs your `code` as the body of an async function with
523	`(bot, mcData, skills, log)` in scope; return a JSON-safe value.
524	
525	```powershell
526	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/eval `
527	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
528	  -d '{"code":"return { pos: bot.entity.position, held: bot.heldItem?.name };"}'
529	```
530	
531	Body: `{code}`. Errors come back as `{"error": "..."}` rather than
532	throwing across the HTTP boundary. There's a 10s soft timeout — if your
533	code is still running past that, the response will note it's still in
534	flight rather than blocking forever. Use this for anything the fixed
535	skills don't cover, and remember the escalation rule above: if you had to
536	reach for `/eval` because a skill failed twice, report it.
537	
538	### `GET /events?since=<n>`
539	
540	Ring buffer (last 500) of notable events: chat heard, health drops,
541	death, kicked, task transitions, quirk hits.
542	
543	```powershell
544	curl.exe -s "http://127.0.0.1:3201/events?since=0"
545	```
546	
547	Response: `{"events":[{"seq":1,"ts":"...","type":"chat","msg":"..."}],
548	"last":42}`. Pass the last `seq` you've seen as `since` next time to get
549	only what's new.
550	
551	## HOME SYSTEM (self-rescue)
552	
553	A server-side datapack (`cavehome`, installed in the world's
554	`datapacks/` folder — not part of this repo) gives every player two
555	legit `/trigger` commands, no admin involvement needed:
556	
557	- `/trigger sethome` — saves the runner's current position as *their
558	  own* home. Per-player automatically (scoreboard-backed, keyed by
559	  username — 8+ bots sharing the server each get their own home, no
560	  collision).
561	- `/trigger home` — teleports the runner back to their saved home. If
562	  no home was ever set, it sends a grey hint instead of erroring:
563	  `[cavehome] no home set yet - run /trigger sethome first.`
564	
565	Drive it exactly like any other chat command, through `/eval` (not
566	`/chat`, since `/trigger` is a raw slash-command, not a talk line):
567	
568	```powershell
569	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/eval `
570	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
571	  -d '{"code":"bot.chat(\"/trigger sethome\")"}'
572	```
573	
574	```powershell

576	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
577	  -d '{"code":"bot.chat(\"/trigger home\")"}'

591	3. **This replaces orchestrator/RCON teleports**, which are now BANNED
592	   (see the superseded tp-rescue policy above) — the bot rescues
593	   *itself* with a command any regular player can run, not an admin
594	   backdoor.
595	4. Still narrate it in chat and report the stuck condition per the

  name: 'fix-staircase-geometry',
  description: 'Root-cause and fix buildStaircase dig-geometry stalls (4 documented failure signatures), adversarially verified',

    { title: 'Understand', detail: '3 parallel readers: algorithm, failure evidence, dependency contracts' },
    { title: 'Design', detail: '2 independent fix designs + judge pick' },
    { title: 'Implement', detail: 'apply winning design to cave/skills.js' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'adversarial signature-trace verify, repair loop until SHIP' },
  ],
}

phase('Understand')
const [algoMap, evidence, contracts] = await parallel([
  () => agent(`Repo: ${REPO}. Read cave/skills.js and produce a COMPLETE technical map of the buildStaircase implementation: the main step loop (how the next step cell is computed each iteration — exact coordinate math), heading selection, the advance-validation checks (including the "cannot advance into step" check), the net-descent watchdog, torch placement, how it calls dig/place/goto helpers, and every guard (dig-law zones, safeDig protections, interior-geometry detection, void-ahead handling). Also map branchMine's descent usage if it shares helpers. Return: structured text map with exact file:line for every piece, plus the exact algorithm expressed as pseudocode faithful to the code. No opinions, just what the code does.`, { model: 'sonnet', phase: 'Understand', label: 'read:algorithm' }),
  () => agent(`Repo: ${REPO}. Read cave/FEEDBACK.md fully and extract EVERY entry about /staircase / buildStaircase failures. There are at least 5: (1) original "step 96, y86->54 claimed, 1 block net descent, ate pickaxe"; (2) interior-start stall (0-1y over 9 steps inside Mine House); (3) clean-ground stall after ~10 real steps when hitting a natural void side; (4) post-dragon-fix stall with barely ANY x/z advance over 9 steps despite real digging (window-1 retry trace with per-15s y polling); (5) "staircase: cannot advance into step at (15,96,43)" rejecting a manually-verified valid cell (air, air above, solid below). Return: numbered failure-signature list, each with its exact ground-truth evidence (coordinates, traces, block states) quoted/condensed from the entries, plus the entry authors' own hypotheses. Include the net-descent watchdog behavior notes (it works — aborts correctly).`, { model: 'sonnet', phase: 'Understand', label: 'read:evidence' }),
  () => agent(`Repo: ${REPO}. Map the helper-layer contracts buildStaircase (cave/skills.js) depends on: gotoLoop/goto helpers + goal classes (cave/movement.js and skills.js usage), the dig helpers (safeDig etc.), placeBlock path (slow-confirm, verify-retry — safePlaceBlock), dig-law zone checks (loadDigZones, isInDigZone, columnEntersDigZone or similar), and position ground-truthing (goalGroundTruth, false-reach catchers in movement.js). For each: signature, semantics, KNOWN QUIRKS from FEEDBACK.md/commit history (goto false-reach, placeBlock false-success, blockAt staleness for unvisited chunks). Return structured contract notes with file:line. Purpose: a designer must know which primitives lie and how.`, { model: 'sonnet', phase: 'Understand', label: 'read:contracts' }),
])

phase('Design')
const designBrief = (angle) => `You are designing a fix for the cavecrew buildStaircase dig-geometry bug. THREE INPUTS:\n\n=== ALGORITHM MAP ===\n${algoMap}\n\n=== FAILURE EVIDENCE (ground truth from live bots) ===\n${evidence}\n\n=== HELPER CONTRACTS + KNOWN LYING PRIMITIVES ===\n${contracts}\n\nDesign angle assigned to you: ${angle}.\n\nProduce: (1) root-cause analysis — for EACH numbered failure signature, name the exact code defect that produces it (or state "cannot explain, needs live probe" honestly); (2) a concrete fix design: which functions change in cave/skills.js, the corrected step-advancement algorithm in precise pseudocode (coordinate math explicit), how each guard/validation changes, how the fix behaves at natural voids and interior starts; (3) risk notes — what could regress (net-descent watchdog must stay, dig-law zones must stay, safeDig protections must stay). The fix must be implementable in cave/skills.js alone. Do NOT write the full code — design-level pseudocode + exact anchor points (file:line from the map).`
const designs = await parallel([
  () => agent(designBrief('CORRECTNESS-FIRST: assume the step-target computation itself is wrong (off-by-one / non-advancing reference position / step-up cancelling step-down). Derive the correct staircase cell sequence from first principles and rebuild the loop math around it.'), { phase: 'Design', label: 'design:math-first', effort: 'high' }),
  () => agent(designBrief('ROBUSTNESS-FIRST: assume the primitives lie (false-reach goto, stale blockAt, false-success place) and the loop lacks ground-truth anchoring. Redesign so every step verifies REAL bot position + REAL block states before/after each dig, resyncing the step cursor to reality instead of trusting internal counters.'), { phase: 'Design', label: 'design:groundtruth-first', effort: 'high' }),
])

const pick = await agent(`Judge two fix designs for the buildStaircase bug. Evidence and constraints:\n\n=== FAILURE EVIDENCE ===\n${evidence}\n\n=== DESIGN A (math-first) ===\n${designs[0]}\n\n=== DESIGN B (groundtruth-first) ===\n${designs[1]}\n\nScore each: does it explain ALL failure signatures? Is the pseudocode implementable in one file? Regression risk? Then produce the FINAL BLUEPRINT: the winning design with the best elements of the loser grafted in — one merged, unambiguous implementation spec (pseudocode + anchor points) an implementer can follow without further judgment calls. State explicitly which signatures the blueprint fixes and which (if any) remain open.`, { phase: 'Design', label: 'judge:blueprint', effort: 'high' })

phase('Implement')
const impl = await agent(`Repo: ${REPO}. Implement this blueprint in cave/skills.js (ONLY this file). Blueprint:\n\n${pick}\n\nRules: preserve net-descent watchdog, dig-law zone checks, safeDig protections, torch placement. Match surrounding code style. Run node --check cave/skills.js until clean. Do NOT commit — leave changes in working tree. Return: summary of every change (file:line), the full new step-loop code section pasted verbatim, node --check result.`, { model: 'sonnet', phase: 'Implement', label: 'implement' })

phase('Verify')
const VERDICT = { type: 'object', properties: { ship: { type: 'boolean' }, findings: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { severity: { type: 'string' }, claim: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['severity', 'claim', 'evidence'] } } }, required: ['ship', 'findings'] }
const verifyPrompt = (lens) => `Repo: ${REPO}. Adversarially verify the UNCOMMITTED buildStaircase changes in cave/skills.js (git diff cave/skills.js). Implementation summary:\n\n${impl}\n\nFailure signatures that MUST be fixed:\n${evidence}\n\nYour lens: ${lens}. Read the actual diff + surrounding code, trace each signature step-by-step against the NEW code (state each trace verdict), hunt regressions (watchdog gone? zone law bypassed? safeDig skipped? infinite loop possible? torch/inventory burn?). ship=false if ANY signature still reproduces on paper or any real regression found. findings: concrete, with code evidence.`
let verdicts = await parallel([
  () => agent(verifyPrompt('geometry correctness — does the step math provably descend and advance on flat ground, at voids, from interior starts'), { phase: 'Verify', label: 'verify:geometry', effort: 'high', schema: VERDICT }),
  () => agent(verifyPrompt('runtime robustness — lying primitives, loop bounds, cancellation, partial-result return, resource burn'), { phase: 'Verify', label: 'verify:robustness', effort: 'high', schema: VERDICT }),
])

let round = 0
while (round < 2) {
  const clean = verdicts.filter(Boolean)
  const blockers = clean.flatMap(v => v.ship ? [] : v.findings.filter(f => f.severity !== 'minor'))
  if (clean.length && blockers.length === 0) break
  round++
  log(`repair round ${round}: ${blockers.length} blocking findings`)
  await agent(`Repo: ${REPO}. Repair these verified findings in the uncommitted cave/skills.js staircase changes (do NOT revert the fix, repair it):\n${JSON.stringify(blockers, null, 2)}\n\nContext: ${impl}\n\nnode --check until clean. No commit. Return change summary.`, { model: 'sonnet', phase: 'Verify', label: `repair:${round}` })
  verdicts = await parallel([
    () => agent(verifyPrompt(`post-repair round ${round} full re-verify, both geometry and robustness`), { phase: 'Verify', label: `reverify:${round}`, effort: 'high', schema: VERDICT }),
  ])
}

const final = verdicts.filter(Boolean)
return {
  ship: final.length > 0 && final.every(v => v.ship),
  remainingFindings: final.flatMap(v => v.findings),
  blueprint: pick.slice(0, 2000),
  implementation: impl.slice(0, 2000),
}

1. **Gemeinsames Repo LEBT**: [monkeorg/tribes-common](https://github.com/monkeorg/tribes-common) — claims-Schema v0, unsere echte Claim-Liste, FEL-Platzhalter (ihre Datei, ihre Hoheit), Grundregeln im README. **Felsen als Maintainer eingeladen**, Ansage in felcrew #50 + Board #6.

{"type":"idle_notification","from":"GrogDriver","timestamp":"2026-09-01T10:41:31.413Z","idleReason":"available","result":"Reported the live trace to team-lead. Quick summary:\n\n**Kit-up complete:** torch 20, spare iron_pickaxe, cobblestone 16, bread 5 (re-withdrawn after idle-guard swept it away), all DEPOT lines sent. Route through the door worked clean, floor patch held up.\n\n**Endpoint correction:** `/buildStaircase` returns 404 — the real endpoint is `/staircase`.\n\n**Staircase run — good news:** descended 15 real levels (y89→74) in 19 steps with genuine digging, 2 torches placed, zero watchdog issues — matches exactly what today's fix was supposed to deliver.\n\n**Then it stopped cleanly** at a genuine natural cave void at (36,72,57) — ground-truth confirmed every neighbor is air, no solid anchor to build a stair tread against. The runner's new void-detection logged it and stopped safely instead of stalling or walking into open air. This looks like the fix working correctly, not a failure.\n\nGrog is safe (HP20/food20, full kit) at (35.7,74,57.5), holding for team-lead's call on how to proceed past the void (bridge it, redirect heading, or something else) — not attempting any workaround on my own per instructions."}
</teammate-message>

<teammate-message teammate_id="Engineer" color="blue" summary="watchCells fix done (15d248f); farm-protection design — needs your call, bigger than small">
Task 2 done: committed 15d248f (watchCells conditional on treadCell, verified both step kinds, node --check clean).

Task 3 (farm-protection) — investigated, this IS bigger-than-small, stopping for your call per your own instruction before implementing.

What exists today: TWO separate zone mechanisms, NEITHER constrains pathfinding itself.
1. cave/zones.json (committed) — a DIG-LAW whitelist (where mining/staircase digging is allowed). Checked at dig-target-selection time (isInDigZone/columnEntersDigZone), never touches travel/goto.
2. local.json's noGoZones (per-machine, circular x/z/radius) — checked at chop/mine TARGET-selection time (isInNoGoZone), also never touches travel/goto.

Neither one is a "pathfinder avoid zone" — a /goto to an unrelated destination (chest C, in Zug's report) has no reason to consult either, and pf's own Movements (runner.js:1138) only knows canDig=false (don't dig NEW openings) — walking ACROSS existing open farmland is normal unblocked movement to pf, same as walking across grass. That's the actual gap.

3 real options, with tradeoffs — didn't want to guess which you want:

A) Block-type avoid (mineflayer-pathfinder's native `Movements.blocksToAvoid` Set, already used for fire/lava/cobweb). Add farmland's block id globally, once, in runner.js's existing Movements setup — smallest possible diff. BUT: (a) it's global — every farm anywhere, forever, not just farm_1, which might be exactly right or might be too broad if we ever want a bot working IN a farm to path across its own plot; (b) I'm not fully certain how blocksToAvoid interacts with a block you're meant to STAND ON TOP OF (it's designed for hazards you'd stand NEAR/avoid touching, like fire — farmland's own boundingBox/physical semantics might not trigger the same avoidance behavior it does for fire). Would need live testing to confirm it actually deters routing rather than no-op'ing.

B) Coordinate-zone via a Movements subclass/getBlock override — the "no_path zone kind in zones.json" you suggested.
